guides.single-narrator.step.1.expected: You have explicitly confirmed the extracted text for this book.
guides.single-narrator.step.1.instructio: Import the book if you have not yet. In the source preview, read the actual extracted text (filename, encoding and excerpt limits are shown; it is the original extracted text, before annotation/preparation), then explicitly confirm the current text. Annotation still runs later and speaker attribution still occurs — this checklist never rewrites dialogue or source words. If the preview is hidden, the guide feedback names the hidden pane: turn off Generate multiple books to show the single-book area; opening this step never changes the book or starts a job.

guides.single-narrator.step.2.cost: Script generation uses your LLM; remote providers may charge.
guides.single-narrator.step.2.expected: A saved script with the intended words and speakers.
guides.single-narrator.step.2.instructio: Generate the annotated script with the existing Generate control. Turn on Preserve source words only through its existing checkbox if you want it. Review speakers against the source before moving on.
guides.single-narrator.step.2.title: Generate and review the script
guides.single-narrator.step.3.cost: Preview may save your already-authorized pending card edits exactly as Voices does, but never applies the book-wide voice. Confirming saves the book-wide voice change; listening/sample playback is separate.
guides.single-narrator.step.3.expected: Every speaker uses the one chosen voice, ready only after your explicit mark.
guides.single-narrator.step.3.instructio: Pick one existing voice on any card (built-in, LoRA, clone or saved-designed — all use the normal Voices resources), then use 'Use this speaker's voice for the book': review every affected speaker and line count, confirm explicitly, and check the ready state in Voices afterwards. Full-cast workflows stay available for other books.
guides.single-narrator.step.3.title: Choose one voice and apply it book-wide
guides.single-narrator.step.4.cost: One row Generate uses TTS. Start one GPU job at a time.
guides.single-narrator.step.4.expected: One listened-to sample for the chosen voice.
guides.single-narrator.step.4.instructio: Press one ordinary row Generate control on a short line, listen with the row player, then mark readiness with the existing Voices Ready controls. A sample is one line only — the remaining lines are generated in the next step. This guide never plays or approves audio for you.
guides.single-narrator.step.4.title: Generate and listen to one sample line
guides.single-narrator.step.5.cost: Render Pending uses TTS/GPU and can take a long time. Cancel with the Cancel button; review saved progress before retrying. The guide never starts it for you.
guides.single-narrator.step.5.expected: Every line has generated audio, or any failures are known and being fixed.
guides.single-narrator.step.5.instructio: Press Render Pending yourself to generate audio for every line that is not done yet (it never replaces finished lines; Regenerate All under Whole-book actions is only for replacing everything). Wait for the Batch complete/incomplete result, then check every line's status. If you press Cancel while it runs or lines fail, fix the cause and press Render Pending again — a cancelled or failed batch is not finished audio. Merge All in the next step only combines chunks that already have audio.
guides.single-narrator.step.5.title: Generate the remaining line audio
guides.single-narrator.step.6.cost: Merging uses CPU and temporary disk space; export has its own Cancel control. A failed or cancelled job is not a finished audiobook. The guide does not press Merge All for you.
guides.single-narrator.step.6.expected: A downloaded file you have actually checked.
guides.single-narrator.step.6.instructio: Press Merge All yourself in Editor (Whole-book actions) after checking line audio and source-match warnings, and wait for the merged result — reaching this step does not mean a merge has happened. Then choose M4B, MP3/WAV chapters or Audacity in Audio, wait for the explicit completion result, download, and play the beginning and ending. An earlier downloaded audiobook will not update itself.

help.action.suggestmorevoices: Generate additional voice candidates for this character to compare.
help.action.suggestvoices: Ask the model to suggest voice assignments for the current characters.
help.action.testllmconnection: Contact the configured model endpoint to check that it can answer a test request.
help.action.testloramodel: Select this adapter in the test-audio controls.
help.action.togglecandidateplayback: Play or stop this saved voice-candidate preview.
help.action.togglechunkexpand: Show or hide this line’s expanded editing controls.
help.action.togglellmkeyvisibility: Show or conceal the API key in this form. This changes its display, not the saved key.
help.action.togglevoicetype: Choose the synthesis mode for this character, such as a stock voice, clone or adapter.
help.action.undosourcescope: Restore the exact previous scope if the saved undo and protected files still match. Later edits can prevent undo.
help.action.uploadclonevoice: Choose a recording to import as this character’s cloning reference.
help.action.uploadloradataset: Upload the selected dataset ZIP so it can be used for adapter training.
help.action.viewreport: Open this saved review report for reading and optional explanation.
help.action.voicechangeshere: Create a voice-change point starting at this line for its character.
help.action.voicelabinspect: Inspect the selected input folder and show which voice datasets are available.
help.changed.dsbupdaterow.emotion: Emotion or delivery style used when synthesizing this sample.
help.changed.dsbupdaterow.seed: Sample seed. Blank or -1 uses the project seed; a non-negative value overrides it.
help.changed.dsbupdaterow.text: Words spoken in this dataset sample.
help.changed.updatechunk.instruct: Delivery or emotion instruction for this script line.
help.changed.updatechunk.pause_after: Pause after this script line, in milliseconds. Leave blank to use the default pause.
help.changed.updatechunk.speaker: Speaker assigned to this script line.
help.changed.updatechunk.style: Style instruction for this script line.
help.changed.updatechunk.text: Words spoken in this script line. Edit the text before regenerating its audio.
help.dynamic.alias-select: Character whose voice settings this name should share as an alias.
help.dynamic.builtin-lora-select: Installed built-in adapter assigned to this character.
help.dynamic.builtin-lora-style: Character-specific style instruction used with the built-in adapter.
help.dynamic.cast-apply-check: Apply the selected saved cast voice to this character.
help.dynamic.cast-apply-target: Saved cast member whose voice should be assigned to this character.
help.dynamic.cast-bulk-check: Include this saved book when applying the selected cast to multiple books.
help.dynamic.cast-list-aliases: Other names for this cast member, separated by commas.
help.dynamic.cast-list-name: Canonical character name or description used in this book’s cast list.
help.dynamic.cast-save-check: Include this character’s configured voice when saving the cast.
help.dynamic.cast-save-scope: Whether this narrator assignment is shared or limited to its displayed scope.
help.dynamic.character-style: Character-specific delivery or accent instructions for the stock voice.
help.dynamic.chunk-instruct: Delivery instruction for this script line’s audio.
help.dynamic.chunk-text: Words spoken in this script line. Saving changes can require regenerating its audio.
help.dynamic.data-apply: Review and confirm saving this one alias in the shared registry for later Review runs. This does not rewrite the current script.
help.dynamic.data-direction: Direction of the proposed alias mapping: the alias will resolve to the selected canonical name.
help.dynamic.data-voice-roster-alias: Canonical character whose voice settings this alias should share.
help.dynamic.data-voice-roster-speaker: Speaker assigned to this script line.
help.dynamic.design-count: Number of voice candidates to design from the chosen line.
help.dynamic.design-description: Base description for this character’s designed voice; per-line delivery notes are appended.
help.dynamic.design-line-select: Character dialogue line used as the spoken sample for voice design.
help.dynamic.designed-voice-select: Saved recording or designed voice used as this character’s cloning reference.
help.dynamic.ensemble-member: Include this character’s assigned voice in the combined ensemble.
help.dynamic.lora-adapter-select: Trained adapter used to synthesize this character’s dialogue.
help.dynamic.lora-character-style: Character-specific style instruction used with the trained adapter.
help.dynamic.nick-alias: Alias or nickname to associate with a canonical character name.
help.dynamic.nick-canonical: Canonical character name that this alias or nickname should resolve to.
help.dynamic.persona-description: Saved persona description associated with this character’s voice.
help.dynamic.ref-audio: Path to the recording used as this character’s cloning reference.
help.dynamic.ref-text: Exact transcript of the cloning reference recording.
help.dynamic.review-batch-check: Include this saved script in the batch review.
help.dynamic.script-batch-upload-check: Include this existing uploaded book in the batch script-generation queue.
help.dynamic.voice-presentation: Optional, user-confirmed description of how this character should sound. Used by model-based voice suggestions; saving it does not change the assigned voice or rendered audio.
help.dynamic.voice-ready: Whether this character’s voice is ready for audio generation.
help.dynamic.voice-seed: Seed for this voice configuration. -1 requests a random seed.
help.dynamic.voice-select: Stock CustomVoice speaker used for this character.
help.dynamic.voice-state-source: Voice assignment used from this character-state boundary onward.
help.dynamic.voice-type: Synthesis mode for this character: stock, built-in adapter, clone, trained adapter, design or ensemble.
help.field.abs-api-key.what: API key for this Audiobookshelf server. Saved in the OS credential store and never returned to the page. Leave blank to keep the stored key.
help.field.abs-author.what: Optional author metadata sent with the audiobook. Leave blank to omit it.
help.field.abs-export-format.what: Choose a completed, current MP3 or M4B export to deliver. The preview checks its saved identity before sending.
help.field.abs-folder.what: Destination folder within the selected library. Preview checks that the folder belongs to that library.
help.field.abs-library.what: Destination library returned by Load libraries. Loading libraries contacts the selected server without uploading audio.
help.field.abs-right-to-share.what: Confirm that you have permission to share the current export and its voices. Confirmation enables Send only after a current preview.
help.field.abs-series.what: Optional series metadata sent with the audiobook. Leave blank to omit it.
help.field.abs-server-url.what: Audiobookshelf server address. Use HTTPS, or HTTP for localhost only. Saving selects the server; it does not upload audio.
help.field.abs-title.what: Title to send with the audiobook. Changing it clears the delivery preview.
help.field.advanced-persona-toggle.what: Advanced persona mode: gathers evidence about each character across the whole script before writing the persona, instead of one sample.
help.field.banned-tokens.what: Comma-separated tokens the model may not produce. To turn reasoning off, use Reasoning effort rather than banning the think tag.
help.field.batch-group-by-type.what: Renders lines grouped by voice type for GPU efficiency, instead of in book order.
help.field.batch-seed.what: Seed for audio generation. A fixed number makes a re-render of the same line repeatable; blank or -1 is random.
help.field.benchmark-manifest.what: JSON object defining benchmark stage, targets, fixtures and settings. It must pass Preflight before Start is enabled.
help.field.calibre-clear-password.what: Clear the stored catalog password when you next save. Use with Load saved settings review before saving again.
help.field.calibre-password.what: Catalog password. Blank keeps the stored password. It is never shown again after saving.
help.field.calibre-root-url.what: Catalog root URL to browse. It is used only after you save the catalog settings; browsing does not save it.
help.field.calibre-username.what: Optional catalog username. Saving stores it with the root URL; browsing contacts the saved catalog only.
help.field.cast-incremental-prompt.what: Literal instructions used only with experimental incremental discovery. Every window still receives all validated names and aliases; source coverage and merge validation remain enforced.
help.field.cast-list-incremental.what: Experimental sequential cast discovery with the complete accumulated roster and aliases. Also adds explicit cast alias evidence to Step 2. Off by default; save configuration before building or generating.
help.field.cast-list-max-tokens.what: Requested reply tokens per cast window, or for the legacy whole-book request. Profile limits still apply; truncated replies are discarded.
help.field.cast-list-source-chars.what: Maximum source characters in each experimental cast window. Instructions and the entire growing roster also need input context. A window that cannot fit stops without publishing a partial cast.
help.field.cast-prompt-preset-select.wha: Saved instructions for building the cast list. Each preset includes whole-book and experimental incremental instructions. Save Setup before starting a build.
help.field.cast-select.what: The saved cast (character → voice mapping) applied to this book.
help.field.cast-whole-book-prompt.what: Literal instructions for whole-book cast discovery. The builder appends the prepared source. Keep the JSON array of name and aliases objects.
help.field.casting-age.what: Show only voices whose description mentions this age group. A voice can carry more than one age group.
help.field.casting-book.what: Show only voices designed for one book. Saved Designer voices are listed under Designer.
help.field.casting-collection-name.what: Name a new voice-library cast to use as a collection. Choose it, then add catalogue voices from their cards.
help.field.casting-collection.what: Collections are existing voice-library casts. Add catalogue clones with a member name, then review mappings before applying to the active book. Existing names are never silently replaced.
help.field.casting-gender.what: Show only voices whose description reads as this gender. Tags come from keywords in the description, not from the audio.
help.field.casting-health.what: Filter missing audio, descriptions, sample lines, duplicate normalized names or skipped folders. Counts cover the whole catalogue. Same-name variants need not be the same speaker.
help.field.casting-review-notes.what: Notes for the voice being reviewed, such as pronunciation or which character it could suit. Save notes keeps them with the voice.
help.field.casting-search.what: Search every designed voice. Words match the name, description and sample line; field:value narrows by book, gender, age, tone, texture, status, priority, tag, source or name, and a leading - excludes.
help.field.casting-sort.what: Order the casting results by name, book, review status or priority.
help.field.casting-status.what: Show only voices with this review status: Unreviewed, Shortlist, Callback or Reject.
help.field.chapter-changed-only.what: Export only chapters whose audio changed since their last export. Turn off for a complete set.
help.field.chapter-format.what: Audio format of the chapter files.
help.field.chapter-padding.what: Zero-padding for chapter numbers in filenames (1, 01 or 001).
help.field.chapter-per-chunk.what: Use the same chapter detection as the M4B export (one chapter per chunk).
help.field.chapter-require-ready.what: Refuse to export until every speaker is marked ready.
help.field.chapter-selection.what: Export only these chapters, e.g. 1, 3, 5-7. Empty exports all.
help.field.chapter-template-preset.what: Saved filename patterns. Pick one to fill the template.
help.field.chapter-template.what: Filename pattern for chapter files. Fields: {chapter_number} {chapter_name} {book_name} {series_name} {volume_number}. The extension is added for you.
help.field.chk-drift-only.what: Show only chunks the drift check flagged as sounding unlike their speaker’s reference voice.
help.field.clone-cleanup-gain.what: Full-length amplitude multiplier from 0.25 to 4.0; 1.0 leaves gain unchanged. It does not trim the reference. A candidate that would clip is refused.
help.field.clone-cleanup-listened-candid: Confirm that you listened to the labelled Candidate and compared it with the Original. This is your listening confirmation, not automated transcript, speaker or quality verification.
help.field.clone-cleanup-listened-origin: Confirm that you listened to the labelled Original reference. This is your listening confirmation, not automated transcript, speaker or quality verification.
help.field.clone-cleanup-remove-dc.what: Optionally remove the constant DC offset before applying gain. This changes the full-length waveform; it does not certify speaker identity, words or quality.
help.field.clone-import-ref-text.what: Exact transcript of the reference recording, including punctuation. It is required for importing the clip.
help.field.clone-import-rights-basis.wha: Optional record of why you may use this recording, such as your own recording, a licence or permission.
help.field.clone-import-rights-confirmed: Confirm that you have permission to use the recording. Import also requires its exact transcript.
help.field.clone-import-source-title.wha: Optional title or description documenting where the reference recording came from.
help.field.clone-import-source-url.what: Optional source link recorded with this reference clip.
help.field.compile-codec.recommend: Leave off: it currently has no effect on render speed.
help.field.compile-codec.what: Compiles the audio codec with torch.compile.
help.field.context-rescue-retries.what: Attempts per context-rescue window before moving to the next, larger one.
help.field.context-rescue-windows.what: When a line can’t be attributed from its chunk, it is retried with this much surrounding text (characters), smallest first.
help.field.date-order-choice.what: How this book reads slash dates that fit both orders, such as 1/2/1900: month first (US) or day first (UK). Auto follows the book's own unambiguous dates, then its spelling, and leaves the date as written when neither decides. Applies to lines rendered from now on; audio already rendered is kept.
help.field.design-alias-select.what: Link this voice to an existing character alias when saving it. None leaves it without an alias link.
help.field.design-description.what: Describe the voice to create, such as its tone, accent and delivery. Generate a new preview after changing this description.
help.field.design-sample-text.what: The words spoken in the designed-voice preview. Changing this text requires a new preview before saving.
help.field.design-text-max-chars.what: Longest character line a persona voice is designed from, up to 500. Longer lines are cut at a sentence end.
help.field.design-text-min-chars.what: Shortest character line a persona voice is designed from. Very short lines like "Okay" make a voice hard to judge and a weak clone reference.
help.field.design-voice-name.what: Name used to save this designed voice so it can be selected again.
help.field.dsb-description.what: Voice description used to synthesize this dataset project’s samples.
help.field.dsb-global-seed.what: Project seed used for dataset generation. Blank or -1 lets the server select a seed; a sample seed of 0 or higher overrides it.
help.field.dsb-project-select.what: Saved dataset-building project to open, including its sample rows and generated audio.
help.field.dsb-ref-select.what: Generated sample selected as the dataset project’s reference clip.
help.field.editor-chapter-regenerate.wha: Also replace audio for lines in these chapters that already have it. Off by default, so only missing lines are rendered. Asks before replacing.
help.field.editor-chapter-selection.what: Chapter numbers to render, as in the Result tab’s chapter box: single numbers and ranges separated by commas, for example 1-3, 5.
help.field.editor-quality-filter.what: Filter the take review queue by saved findings, historical speech evidence or missing checks. Compare retained candidates without changing audio; restoration requires an explicit action. Unknown evidence is not a clean result.
help.field.editor-repair-chapter.what: Choose one detected export chapter, or the entire book, for the audio repair preview. Without headings, the whole script is one chapter.
help.field.editor-repair-speakers.what: Select one or more literal speaker labels to include in the repair preview. Preview shows the exact affected lines before audio replacement.
help.field.epub-extraction-report-enable: Include a page-local EPUB import snapshot of source hashes, reading order and extraction decisions. It does not change speech text. Paths and chapter labels may be private; incomplete detail is marked. Re-upload to inspect another source revision.
help.field.existing-upload-select.what: Reuse a book uploaded earlier instead of uploading it again.
help.field.export-mastering-enabled.what: Opt in to measured loudness and true-peak processing for the next assembled export. Does not alter source clips or start a job.
help.field.export-mastering-loudness.wha: Target integrated loudness, from -24 to -14 LUFS. Check the measured final file; a target alone does not establish compliance.
help.field.export-mastering-peak.what: Target true-peak ceiling, from -9 to -1 dBTP. Lossy encoding may change the achieved peak; compare final measurements.
help.field.export-quality-gap.what: Minimum unexpected silent interval reported during the next assembled export, in seconds. It warns by default; enable rejection to refuse these gaps before replacing a delivery.
help.field.export-quality-noise.what: Level below which every audio channel counts as silent during the next MP3, M4B or chapter check. Authored pauses are excluded; Audacity checks track structure instead.
help.field.export-quality-reject.what: Refuse the next MP3, M4B or chapter export if an unexpected long silent interval is detected. Leave unchecked for advisory results. Failed attempts preserve earlier deliveries.
help.field.file-upload.what: Text, Markdown, EPUB or DOCX policy v2: body paragraphs, known metadata and checked style inheritance. DOCX requires preview and Accept; original, text and receipt are retained. Unsupported structures refuse. No inference starts. Inspect retained DOCX files for metadata and offline cleanup guidance.
help.field.llm-api-retry-limit.what: How many times a failed API call (connection error, rate limit, server error) is retried before giving up. Blank uses each stage’s default.
help.field.llm-connect-timeout.what: How long to wait to open a connection. Blank uses the request timeout.
help.field.llm-context-length.what: Profile token budget for prompt and reply. A lower detected context still wins. Reducing this caps requests; it does not unload the model or free GPU memory.
help.field.llm-failover.what: If this profile gives up (retries exhausted or a content-policy refusal), the rest of the run switches to the other profile. You are asked to confirm first when that would use a billed endpoint.
help.field.llm-key.what: API key sent with each request. Local servers usually accept any value. Use env:NAME to read it from an environment variable instead of saving it.
help.field.llm-max-input-tokens.what: Largest prompt this profile may send. Blank inherits the global input ceiling. Lower it for providers with a smaller input limit.
help.field.llm-max-output-tokens.what: Largest reply this profile may request. Blank means no profile cap; each task still has its own safety ceiling.
help.field.llm-mode.what: Which LLM profile is active: Local (this machine) or Remote (a server elsewhere). Each profile keeps its own address, model and limits.
help.field.llm-model.what: Model name sent with each request. It must match a model the server has loaded or offers.
help.field.llm-on-api-exhaustion.what: What happens when API retries run out: fail that chunk, or pause the run so you can fix the server and Resume from the same request.
help.field.llm-on-this-gpu.what: Whether the LLM shares this machine’s GPU with audio generation. If not, script work can run while audio renders instead of waiting for the card. Auto treats a local address as yes and a remote one as no.
help.field.llm-provider-extra-body.what: Extra JSON fields merged into every request body, for provider-specific options. Output-size fields here are still capped by the task limits.
help.field.llm-provider-headers.what: Extra HTTP headers (a JSON object) sent with every request, for providers that need them. Leave empty otherwise.
help.field.llm-reasoning-effort.recommen: medium on a base model when time allows: minor-character attribution rose 57 → 63% at about 3× the time.
help.field.llm-reasoning-effort.source: RECIPES.md → Prompt (reasoning on the base model)
help.field.llm-reasoning-effort.what: Sent as reasoning_effort on every request from this profile, for models that think before answering. Server default leaves it unset.
help.field.llm-request-interval.what: Minimum seconds between requests. Use it to stay under a provider rate limit; 0 sends as fast as replies arrive.
help.field.llm-request-timeout.what: How long to wait for a reply before treating the request as failed. Blank uses the app default. Raise it for slow models on long chunks.
help.field.llm-retry-initial-delay.what: Wait before the first API retry, in seconds. Later retries multiply it by the backoff multiplier.
help.field.llm-retry-jitter.what: Randomises each retry wait by ± this fraction so parallel workers do not retry at the same moment.
help.field.llm-retry-max-delay.what: Upper limit on the wait between API retries, in seconds.
help.field.llm-retry-multiplier.what: Each API retry waits this many times longer than the last.
help.field.llm-ssh.what: SSH host alias for the remote machine. Only the Optimize button uses it, to reconfigure a remote LM Studio.
help.field.llm-transport.what: Send requests to the server above, or Manual: each request appears on the Script tab for you to answer elsewhere and paste back. The reply is checked exactly as a model’s would be.
help.field.llm-url.what: Address of the OpenAI-compatible server (LM Studio, llama.cpp, Ollama, a hosted API), ending in /v1.
help.field.lmstudio-optimize-toggle.what: Reloads LM Studio with tuned settings: locally context 8192 and parallel 1 (kept low for VRAM safety); remotely context 98304 and parallel 2 over SSH. Off restores LM Studio’s defaults.
help.field.lora-adapter-name.what: Name of the LoRA adapter created by this training run.
help.field.lora-alpha.what: Scaling factor applied to LoRA updates relative to the adapter rank.
help.field.lora-batch-size.what: Number of training samples processed together in a step. Larger batches require more memory.
help.field.lora-dataset-file.what: Training-dataset ZIP to upload. Upload it before selecting it for training.
help.field.lora-dataset-select.what: Uploaded dataset whose audio and transcripts will be used to train this adapter.
help.field.lora-epochs.what: Number of full passes through the selected training dataset.
help.field.lora-grad-accum.what: Number of steps whose gradients are accumulated before a weight update. Effective batch size is batch size multiplied by this value.
help.field.lora-language.what: Language token used during training. Choose the language of the dataset recordings.
help.field.lora-lr.what: Learning rate: the size of each training weight update.
help.field.lora-rank.what: Capacity of the LoRA adapter. It also affects adapter size and training memory use.
help.field.lora-test-adapter.what: Trained adapter to use when generating test audio.
help.field.lora-test-instruct.what: Optional delivery instruction for test audio, such as warm or gentle narration.
help.field.lora-test-text.what: Words to synthesize for the selected adapter test.
help.field.m4b-author.what: Author written into the M4B metadata.
help.field.m4b-cover-input.what: Cover image embedded in the M4B.
help.field.m4b-description.what: Short description written into the M4B metadata.
help.field.m4b-narrator.what: Narrator credit written into the M4B metadata.
help.field.m4b-per-chunk.what: One M4B chapter per chunk instead of grouping by detected chapter headings.
help.field.m4b-publication-author-choice: Choose an author suggestion for an untouched blank Author field. Entered or intentionally cleared authors are kept.
Select the captured cover for export without replacing an uploaded cover asset.
help.field.m4b-publication-origin.what: Choose an exact captured EPUB origin. Identical extracted text can have different publication metadata.
help.field.m4b-publication-reviewed.what: Confirm you reviewed the origin and stale or ambiguous details. Source capture does not certify script wording.
Choose a title suggestion for an untouched blank Title field. Entered or intentionally cleared titles are kept.
help.field.m4b-require-ready.what: Refuse to export until every speaker is marked ready.
help.field.m4b-title.what: Book title written into the M4B metadata. An untouched blank uses Audiobook; clearing an entered title or choosing Leave empty omits it.
help.field.m4b-year.what: Year written into the M4B metadata.
help.field.manual-copy-text.what: Read-only text for manual copying when the browser refuses automatic clipboard access.
help.field.manual-llm-reply.what: Paste only the answer to the current manual request. Submit checks it against that request before the waiting task continues.
help.field.max-input-tokens.what: Largest prompt any profile may send. Blank keeps the existing context checks. A profile’s own input ceiling overrides it.
help.field.max-tokens.what: Starting reply size for LLM requests. A verified larger context can raise it up to each task’s safety ceiling; a profile output ceiling caps it.
help.field.merge-narrators.what: During review, joins neighbouring NARRATOR lines that share a delivery note into one longer line. Leave off for finer per-line voice control.
help.field.min-p.what: Tokens less likely than this fraction of the top token are dropped. 0 disables it.
help.field.narrator-focus.what: Character whose narrator variant is previewed.
help.field.narrator-strategy.what: How the narrator voice is chosen: one global voice, or varied by scene focus, chapter, focus character, or the character’s gender and age.
help.field.parallel-workers.what: How many TTS requests run at once. More can be faster on a large GPU or server pool, but uses more memory.
help.field.pass1-prompt-preset-select.wh: Prompt preset for Step 1 (splitting text into lines). Default uses the checked-in prompt.
help.field.pass1-system-prompt.what: Step 1 system prompt. Edit only to customise; the text must still come back word for word.
help.field.pass1-user-prompt.what: Step 1 user prompt template. It must keep {chunk}.
help.field.pass3-prompt-preset-select.wh: Prompt preset for Step 3 (delivery notes). Default uses the checked-in prompt.
help.field.pass3-system-prompt.what: Step 3 system prompt for writing delivery notes.
help.field.pass3-user-prompt.what: Step 3 user prompt template. It must keep {batch}.
help.field.pause-between-speakers.what: Silence inserted when the speaker changes, in milliseconds, when audio is merged.
help.field.pause-same-speaker.what: Silence inserted between consecutive lines by the same speaker, in milliseconds.
help.field.persona-advanced-prompt.what: Template for the advanced persona compilation. It uses {character_ref}.
help.field.persona-batch-size.what: Script lines per persona-evidence request in advanced mode.
help.field.persona-context-custom.what: Custom number of sample spoken lines per character included in the persona prompt.
help.field.persona-context-lines.what: Number of sample spoken lines per character included in the persona prompt.
help.field.persona-recovery-json.what: The persona JSON reply you got from another LLM, pasted here to validate and save.
help.field.persona-recovery-narration.wh: Narration context included when you copy the persona prompt.
help.field.persona-recovery-samples.what: Dialogue samples included when you copy the persona prompt.
help.field.persona-recovery-speaker.what: The character whose persona you are recovering by hand.
help.field.persona-recovery-state.what: Save the recovered persona for the base character or one of its states.
help.field.persona-reference-chars.what: How much character evidence the advanced persona compilation may send per request. The model’s context may force smaller requests.
help.field.persona-system-prompt.what: System instruction for voice-persona generation, shared by basic and advanced modes.
help.field.persona-unknown-network-conte: Use the allowance above for network models whose context size is unknown. Turn on only if the provider supports large requests; rejections fall back to smaller batches.
help.field.persona-user-prompt.what: Template for a basic persona. It uses {speaker}, {narrator_context} and {sample_lines}.
help.field.prep-allow-cpu-fallback.what: Permit enrichment on the CPU when GPU support is unavailable. CPU enrichment can take substantially longer.
help.field.prep-audio-file.what: WAV or MP3 recording to transcribe and split into a voice-training dataset.
help.field.prep-batch-files.what: Choose the recordings to prepare as separate datasets in batch mode.
help.field.prep-batch-mode.what: Prepare several audio files as separate training datasets. Batch mode uses the shared language, confidence, noise and diarization settings.
help.field.prep-batch-size.what: Number of chunks grouped into an LLM annotation batch during single-file preparation.
help.field.prep-chunk-size.what: Target duration in seconds for audio chunks produced during preparation.
help.field.prep-confidence.what: Minimum average word-alignment confidence from 0 to 1 for keeping a chunk. Higher values reject more chunks.
help.field.prep-diarization-mode.what: Off skips speaker separation. Auto checks for multiple speakers; Always diarize runs speaker separation regardless.
help.field.prep-enrich-emotion.what: Include emotional-tone descriptions in LLM enrichment.
help.field.prep-enrich-narration.what: Include narration-style descriptions in LLM enrichment.
help.field.prep-enrich-speaker.what: Include speaker-attribution information in LLM enrichment.
help.field.prep-enrich-with-llm.what: Run the optional LLM enrichment stage and show its speaker, narration-style and emotion settings.
help.field.prep-fallback-model.what: Optional fallback GGUF model path for annotation during preparation.
help.field.prep-hf-token.what: Hugging Face token with access to the diarization model. It is used for this run and is not saved.
help.field.prep-keep-unaligned.what: Keep chunks that fail source matching instead of dropping them. Their text may need inspection before training.
help.field.prep-lang.what: Language of the recording being prepared for training.
help.field.prep-llm-model-path.what: GGUF model path for the optional enrichment stage.
help.field.prep-min-chunk-duration.what: Shortest audio chunk to keep, in seconds. Shorter chunks are discarded.
help.field.prep-model.what: Optional primary GGUF model path used for annotation during preparation. Blank uses the configured default.
help.field.prep-no-auto-anchor.what: Disable automatic selection of a starting anchor in the source text.
help.field.prep-output.what: Filename of the training-dataset ZIP produced by single-file preparation.
help.field.prep-resume.what: Resume preparation using the existing dataset_temp working files instead of starting the single-file run from scratch.
help.field.prep-snr.what: Minimum signal-to-noise ratio in decibels for keeping a chunk. Higher values reject noisier audio.
help.field.prep-source-file.what: Optional EPUB or text file matching the recording, used for source-guided chunking and alignment recovery.
help.field.prep-source-start-text.what: Find this text in the source and use it as the alignment starting point.
help.field.prep-source-start.what: Word position in the source text where alignment should begin.
help.field.prep-source-threshold.what: Minimum source-match ratio from 0 to 1. Matching chunks use source spelling; lower-scoring chunks are dropped unless Keep unaligned chunks is enabled.
help.field.presence-penalty.what: Discourages repeating tokens that already appeared. 0 disables it.
help.field.preset-editor-description.wha: Optional note describing when to use this preset.
help.field.preset-editor-name.what: Name of the preset to save. An existing name replaces that saved preset.
help.field.prompt-example.what: Worked example shown to the model before the roster. Used by the michel2_shot preset.
help.field.prompt-preset-select.recommen: michel2_spoken on Qwen3-14B without an adapter: +6.5 points on a local gold set (p = 0.001) with about 3× less Step 2 time. Not yet measured on other models.
help.field.prompt-preset-select.what: How Step 2 asks the model who speaks each line. michel2_full is the default. michel2_spoken labels only the quotes and fills narration in code. If you serve an attribution adapter, keep the prompt it was trained on (usually michel2_full).
help.field.pronunciation-audition-origin: Short original spelling to audition literally, without applying saved pronunciation substitutions. Generates temporary audio only.
help.field.pronunciation-audition-spoken: Short proposed spoken replacement, applied to the original spelling through normal speech preparation with the selected line voice. Listening decides whether the replacement helps.
help.field.pronunciation-line.what: Choose a current script line whose assigned voice, narrator context and voice timeline will be used for disposable pronunciation auditions.
help.field.readalong-include-text.what: Include the script text in the downloadable sidecar. Unchecked sidecars contain timings only.
help.field.readaloud-timing-device.what: Choose where Qwen alignment runs. Auto uses an eligible GPU or CPU. A GPU build reserves the shared GPU lock; wait for other GPU work to finish. Chunk timing always uses CPU.
help.field.readaloud-timing-language.wha: Speech language for Qwen alignment. EPUB language reads the retained book metadata. Choose an override when metadata is wrong or unavailable; unsupported languages are refused. Chunk timing has no aligner-language limit.
help.field.readaloud-timing-mode.what: Choose EPUB timing. Auto uses Qwen3 when its isolated runtime and model are ready; otherwise it uses CPU chunk timing. Qwen estimates sentence times. Chunk uses editor chunk bounds and needs no extra model. See docs/readalong.md for installation.
help.field.reproducible-takes.what: Regenerating an unchanged line gives the same take, and the Editor shows a Different take button for a new one. Covers one-at-a-time renders only; batch renders share one random state.
help.field.review-batch-bidirectional.wh: Runs nickname discovery forward and then backward, so early books pick up names that are explained later. Needs nickname discovery; about twice the time.
help.field.review-batch-context-window.w: 0 runs the standard review. Above 0, each line is reviewed with that many neighbouring lines on each side.
help.field.review-batch-find-nicknames.w: Before merging names, discovers each book’s nicknames and shares them across the series.
help.field.review-batch-mode.what: Review several saved books in one run instead of the current one.
help.field.review-context-window.what: Neighbouring lines shown on each side of every reviewed line, so review can fix boundaries and speakers using the surrounding scene.
help.field.review-dedupe-speakers.what: Merges different names for the same character (e.g. a first name and a full name) into one speaker and voice.
help.field.review-force-rerun.what: Review again even if nothing changed since the last completed review.
help.field.review-system-prompt.what: Instructions for the review pass: which mistakes to fix and how.
help.field.review-user-prompt.what: Template for each review batch. It must keep {context} and {batch}.
help.field.roster-consent.what: Confirm that you reviewed the proposed identities and exact source locations. Edits invalidate this confirmation.
help.field.roster-import.what: Choose an exported approved character roster. Review every imported identity and quote against the selected book before approval.
help.field.roster-split-name.what: Name the new character when splitting one selected identity. Supply a supporting source quote before approval.
help.field.roster-split-new.what: Retire the original identity and allocate two new identities for this split. Leave off to keep the original identity for one character.
help.field.roster-survivor.what: Choose which selected existing identity survives a merge. Other merged identities are retired.
help.field.save-script-name.what: Name to save the current script under in the script library.
help.field.script-batch-build-cast-lists: On: in an A/B on 5 PDNC books, unnamed speakers went from 0% to 72% correct and named speakers from 69% to 93%.
Builds a cast list for each book that has none first, one extra request per book, so unnamed speakers get their own label instead of UNKNOWN.
help.field.script-batch-files.what: The books for a multi-book run: text, Markdown or EPUB. DOCX batch import is unsupported; preview and accept DOCX individually first.
help.field.script-batch-mode.what: Generate scripts for several books in one run instead of one.
help.field.script-collision-policy.what: What a multi-book run does when a book already has a saved script: skip it, save a new version, or back up and replace it.
For books narrated in the first person: the narrator’s exact character name, so their narration and dialogue get one voice. Leave empty otherwise.
help.field.script-literal-source-preserv: Keeps the book’s exact words through annotation and review. Numbers and symbols may still be expanded later for speech.
help.field.script-strip-front-matter.wha: Removes known non-story boilerplate (translator’s notes, tables of contents) before the text is sent to the LLM.
help.field.setup-expert-toggle.what: Show the advanced Setup categories: limits and retries, audio and timing, generation, script strategy and prompt studio. Switching it off changes no setting and saves nothing.
help.field.setup-settings-category.what: Choose which Setup category to display. Edits in other categories are retained. Save Configuration applies all edited categories.
help.field.setup-settings-search.what: Find available Setup settings by their labels and explanations, then jump to the original control. Does not search field values or save settings.
help.field.setup-ui-locale.what: Choose the language of this Setup pane and the app shell: English, Chinese, Japanese, Spanish or the layout-test Pseudo-English. Help text, task logs, safety warnings and other tabs stay English until their phase ships. Preserves counts, config values and book/TTS/transcription language.
help.field.single-voice-source.what: Speaker whose existing voice to review for book-wide use. Preview lists every affected speaker before anything is applied.
help.field.sound-assets-file.what: Choose WAV, FLAC, MP3 or OGG audio to retain in the sound asset library. Import verifies the complete file. It does not change book audio; use the library to audition it first.
help.field.source-preview-confirm.what: Confirms the loaded source-text excerpt snapshot for the current book in this tab. Reload the preview to check the current source.
help.field.source-scope-entry.what: Choose the first saved entry to retain. Preview checks the exact source words, chunk boundary, voices and saved audio before any change.
help.field.source-scope-search.what: Find a saved entry by its heading or words. Search does not change the book.
help.field.speaker-review-consent.what: Confirms that the shown book and reference excerpts may be sent to this model endpoint. Remote providers may charge for it.
help.field.speaker-review-max-pairs.what: Most label pairs sent for review in one run (up to 20).
help.field.speaker-review-partial.what: Allow reviewing labels from an attribution checkpoint that has not finished.
help.field.speaker-review-reference.what: A saved script to compare the labels against, used as a provisional reference.
help.field.speaker-review-source.what: Which speaker labels to check: the current script or an attribution checkpoint.
help.field.speech-retry-enabled.what: Off by default; save with speech checks enabled. Retry confirmed missing/extra speech once with a new seed. Unavailable or review keeps prior audio and never retries; with no prior take the line errors with no audio. Adds time; native batches run one line at a time. Not listening acceptance.
help.field.speech-verification-enabled.w: Check new English takes with cached CPU ASR and short-line acoustics. Off by default; save to apply. Confirmed missing or extra speech rejects the attempt and keeps the prior take. Unsupported or unavailable checks are labeled. Adds time and RAM; listening review is still needed.
help.field.sub-batch-enabled.what: Splits a batch by text length so short lines are not padded to the length of long ones.
help.field.sub-batch-max-items.what: Hard cap on lines per sub-batch. 0 picks a size from the VRAM estimate.
help.field.sub-batch-min-size.what: A batch is only split once it has at least this many chunks.
help.field.sub-batch-ratio.what: A batch is split when its longest line is more than this many times its shortest.
help.field.synthesis-clause-gap.what: Optional target silence at clause joins within one take. Blank preserves natural silence; trimming is limited by the edge trim setting.
help.field.synthesis-crossfade.what: Overlap adjacent continuation windows by up to this duration, bounded by available audio. Zero disables crossfading. Listen to check the resulting join.
help.field.synthesis-edge-trim.what: Maximum detected quiet audio removed from each internal boundary edge. Zero preserves the original edges, and the outer line edges are always kept.
help.field.synthesis-fade.what: Short fade at internal sentence, clause and paragraph boundaries. Zero disables fading. Listen to check consonants and endings after changing this value.
help.field.synthesis-paragraph-gap.what: Optional target silence at paragraph joins within one take. Blank preserves natural silence; trimming is limited by the edge trim setting.
help.field.synthesis-quiet-threshold.wha: Optional silence detection threshold from -120 to 0 dBFS. Blank uses the existing threshold. Quiet speech can require a lower value.
help.field.synthesis-recovery-budget.wha: Logical limit for indexed recovery audio across the workspace, in MiB (16–4096). Default 256. Interrupted cache writes remain charged; temporary working files are separate.
help.field.synthesis-recovery-enabled.wh: Keep verified windows for interrupted fixed-seed native local stock-voice renders on Linux. Off by default. Save Configuration to apply; unsupported renders continue normally and selected takes are preserved.
help.field.synthesis-sentence-gap.what: Optional target silence at sentence joins within one take. Blank preserves natural silence; trimming is limited by the edge trim setting.
help.field.synthesis-windows-enabled.wha: Use explicit limits to synthesize smaller windows inside a line. Save Configuration to apply these choices to future renders.
help.field.system-prompt.what: Attribution instruction block. Default-shaped prompts must keep {roster} and {batch}; passage-shaped prompts (michel, michel2…) get the roster and marked passage added around them.
help.field.temperature.what: Sampling randomness for single-pass generation and review. 0 always picks the most likely token. The three-pass steps have their own temperatures below.
help.field.top-k.what: Only the K most likely tokens are considered. 0 disables it.
help.field.top-p.what: Nucleus sampling: only tokens within this cumulative probability are considered.
help.field.tp-attribute-batch-size.recom: 25, the size every attribution measurement used.
help.field.tp-attribute-batch-size.what: How many lines Step 2 sends together when deciding who speaks.
help.field.tp-attribute-context-chars.wh: Extra book text shown before and after each Step 2 request, as evidence only. Each 1,000 characters adds about 300 tokens per request.
help.field.tp-attribute-target-chars.wha: Size Step 2 requests by characters instead of line count. 0 keeps line-based batching.
help.field.tp-chunk-size.what: How much book text Step 1 sends per request when splitting it into lines. Bigger pieces mean fewer requests, but a longer reply that is redone whole if one word comes back wrong.
help.field.tp-delivery-direction.recomme: Current notes. The experimental modes need the default Step 3 prompt preset, and changing this restarts an unfinished book instead of resuming it.
help.field.tp-delivery-direction.what: For the Step 3 notes: keep today’s notes (Current) or ask the model to also say how each line answers the one before it and to mark pauses (a beat, a cut-off, trailing off) that become silence between lines. The experimental modes are being evaluated in a blind listening test and are off by default.
help.field.tp-group-rule.what: Unnamed dialogue from a group on the cast list (e.g. THE GUARDS) is assigned to that group instead of UNKNOWN.
help.field.tp-instruct-context-chars.rec: 0. In a blind review the default never lost to the old behaviour, and no non-zero value was better.
help.field.tp-instruct-context-chars.wha: Extra book text shown around each Step 3 (delivery notes) request.
help.field.tp-instruct-target-chars.what: Size Step 3 requests by characters instead of line count. 0 keeps line-based batching.
help.field.tp-keep-whole-batch.what: Keeps a Step 2 batch whose only problems are names written in lower case in the book or an unnamed quoted line. Those lines are marked for review instead of re-asked.
help.field.tp-pass1-format.recommend: Full text. Compact used fewer tokens but scored a little lower on clean books.
help.field.tp-pass1-format.what: For chunks the quote marks don’t settle: rewrite the text (Full) or label numbered sentences (Compact, experimental, which falls back to Full on any unusable reply).
help.field.tp-quoted-must-be-spoken.what: Rejects a Step 1 reply that types quoted text as narration.
help.field.tp-segment-output-ratio.what: Step 1’s reply budget as a multiple of the text sent. Raise it for models that write a lot of formatting around the text.
help.field.tp-segment-temperature.what: Sampling randomness for Step 1 (splitting text into lines).
help.field.tp-segmentation.recommend: Quote marks first, model for the rest. Every three-pass result was measured with it, and books with em-dash or unmarked dialogue need it.
help.field.tp-segmentation.what: How Step 1 finds the dialogue: from quote marks, from the model, or both.
help.field.tp-speaker-traits.what: Also records gender, age group and ageless status for each line. This adds to every Step 2 reply; check the inferred traits against the book.
Rejects a Step 1 reply that types unquoted text as speech.
help.field.translated-edition-pair.what: Choose one installed language pair for the translation preview. Only directly installed pairs are listed; nothing is downloaded and no language setting changes.
help.field.tts-device.what: Where the local TTS model runs. Auto picks the best available GPU, else the CPU.
help.field.tts-external-server-number.wh: Select the saved external server to inspect, numbered from 1 in saved pool order. The check reads schema only; it does not save settings or generate audio.
help.field.tts-external-timeout.what: A line that takes longer than this on an external server is marked failed instead of waited on.
help.field.tts-external-urls.what: Extra external TTS servers, one per line. Batch rendering spreads lines across them. Empty uses only the address above.
help.field.tts-language.what: Language the audio is spoken in. It does not change script generation; edit the prompts for that.
help.field.tts-max-new-tokens.what: Upper limit on audio generated per chunk. Too low cuts long lines short; lower values fit bigger batches.
help.field.tts-mode.what: Local loads the built-in Qwen3-TTS model on this machine. External sends lines to a running Gradio TTS server. Apple MLX (experimental) runs Qwen3-TTS on Apple Silicon Macs in the separate mlx_env that Install creates; it supports custom, cloned, designed and LoRA voices (ensembles need Local).
help.field.tts-url.what: Address of the external Qwen3-TTS Gradio server.
help.field.user-prompt.what: Attribution user instruction. The pipeline fills {roster} and {batch}.
help.field.vl-candidate-checkpoints.what: Number of retained checkpoint candidates requested for evaluation, up to two. Zero requests no candidate checkpoints.
help.field.vl-device.what: Device requested for pipeline model work: automatic selection, CUDA or CPU.
help.field.vl-epub_dirs.what: Folders searched for EPUB prose context when generating voice descriptions. Enter one folder per line.
help.field.vl-lora-r.what: Rank of the adapter trained by Voice Lab, controlling its capacity and memory requirements.
help.field.vl-max-epochs.what: Maximum number of passes through each voice dataset before training stops.
help.field.vl-name-apply.what: Allow the naming stage to rename adapters. Unchecked produces a dry-run preview.
help.field.vl-name-overwrite.what: Allow the naming stage to replace descriptive names that adapters already have.
help.field.vl-profiler_model.what: Optional GGUF model used to write voice profiles. Blank uses the profiler default.
help.field.vl-rocm_python.what: Python interpreter used by the Voice Lab pipeline. It needs the dependencies required by the selected stages.
help.field.vl-stage-dedup.what: Cluster voices, merge confirmed matches and remove exact duplicate clips before training.
help.field.vl-stage-evaluate.what: Generate fixed evaluation probes and report speaker-similarity, silence and clipping warnings.
help.field.vl-stage-name.what: Create descriptive voice names and, when enabled below, rename the adapters.
help.field.vl-stage-profile.what: Build acoustic and LLM descriptions of the voices.
help.field.vl-stage-quality.what: Audit clip health and duplicate evidence. This stage reports warnings rather than silently removing clips.
help.field.vl-stage-train.what: Train a LoRA adapter for each deduplicated voice dataset.
help.field.vl-target-loss.what: Stop training early when average training loss reaches this target or lower. Loss alone does not establish voice quality.
help.field.vl-zips_dir.what: Dataset input folder for this pipeline run, containing narrator subfolders.
help.field.vl-zips_dir_cfg.what: Default dataset input folder saved in the Voice Lab pipeline settings.
help.field.voices-keep-in-library.what: Save the current voices to the library before they are replaced.
help.field.voices-scope.what: Assign voices only to characters that have none, or to every character (replacing current voices).
help.field.voices-state-filter.what: Show all characters, or only those with or without state cards (per-state voices, e.g. a time skip).

help.item.btn-merge: Merge generated chunk audio into the combined output using the configured pauses.
help.item.btn-review-script: Review the current annotated script with the configured model and review settings.
help.item.btn-review-script-contextual: Review script entries with surrounding context using the selected context-window setting.
help.item.candidate-in-use: This saved voice candidate is already assigned to the character.
help.item.cast-row-remove: Remove this cast-list row from the editor. Save the cast list to retain the edit.
help.item.cast-save-threshold: Minimum line count used to preselect characters whose voices will be saved to this cast.
help.item.casting-clear: Clear the search, dropdown filters and tone or texture chips.
help.item.casting-create-collection: Create a voice-library cast with the collection name, then choose catalogue voices to add to it.
help.item.casting-match-collection: Review character mappings from this collection for the active book before applying them. Nothing is applied until you confirm.
help.item.casting-play-all: Play every matching voice that has preview audio, one after another. Press again to stop.
help.item.casting-refresh: Reload the casting library from the designed voices on disk, including review marks.
help.item.casting-review: Review the matching voices one at a time, starting with the first unreviewed one.
help.item.casting-review-callback: Mark this voice Callback and move to the next one.
help.item.casting-review-next: Go to the next voice in this review.
help.item.casting-review-play: Play or stop this voice preview.
help.item.casting-review-prev: Go back to the previous voice in this review.
help.item.casting-review-reject: Mark this voice Reject and move to the next one.
help.item.casting-review-save-notes: Save the notes for this voice.
help.item.casting-review-shortlist: Mark this voice Shortlist and move to the next one.
help.item.casting-view-cards: Show the matching voices as cards with their description and controls.
help.item.casting-view-table: Show the matching voices as a compact table.
help.item.chapter-export-btn: Export the selected chapters into individual audio files.
help.item.chapter-preset-import: Choose a JSON file containing chapter filename presets to import.
help.item.chapter-preview-btn: Preview chapter boundaries and filenames for the current export settings.
help.item.chunk-generate: Generate this script line’s audio using its current text, delivery and assigned voice.
help.item.clone-cleanup-accept: After transcript, rights and both listening confirmations, accept the verified candidate as a new immutable reference. The selected voice does not change automatically.
help.item.clone-cleanup-prepare: Prepare and verify a separate full-length candidate using the selected gain and DC options. This does not import it or change the selected voice.
help.item.clone-cleanup-reject: Discard the pending preview if present; already accepted voices remain in the library. The selected voice and source recording are unchanged.
help.item.clone-import-submit: Validate the transcript and permission confirmation, then import this reference recording.
help.item.config-save-button: Save the current configuration so subsequent tasks use these settings.
help.item.config-save-button-top: Save the current configuration so subsequent tasks use these settings.
help.item.confirmmodalcancel: Dismiss this confirmation without performing the proposed action.
help.item.confirmmodalok: Confirm the specific action described in this dialog.
help.item.dataset-builder-link: Open the Dataset tab to build a new training dataset.
help.item.download-file: Download this file to your computer.
help.item.dsb-btn-gen-all: Generate audio for dataset sample rows that still need it.
help.item.dsb-btn-regen-all: Regenerate audio for every sample row in the selected dataset project.
help.item.dsb-import-button: Choose sample definitions in a JSON file to import into this dataset project.
help.item.editor-chapter-refresh: Reload the chapter progress map from the current lines.
help.item.editor-chapter-start: Render the chosen chapters with the current voices and settings. Other chapters’ audio is left as it is.
help.item.editor-drawer-scrim: Dims the page while the tool drawer is open. Clicking it closes the drawer and returns focus to the Tools button.
help.item.editor-line-waveform-retry: Try reading the selected take again after a waveform error. This only refreshes the sketch; it does not regenerate or change the audio.
help.item.editor-tools-close: Close the tool drawer and return focus to the Tools button. Closing changes no setting and discards nothing.
help.item.editor-tools-toggle: Open or close the tool drawer, which keeps the sound, rendition, mix, pronunciation, chapter and repair panels beside the line editor without leaving this tab.
help.item.llm-model-refresh: Ask the configured endpoint for its served model names and update the model picker.
help.item.lora-comparison-close: Close the adapter comparison or listening-review panel.
help.item.manual-retained-reply: Read-only copy of an earlier model reply, retained so an unsent response is not lost.
help.item.media-preview: Play, pause or seek through this media preview and adjust its volume. Playback does not regenerate the audio.
help.item.modal-dismiss: Close this dialog without confirming its pending action.
help.item.navbar-collapse: Show or hide the app navigation menu.
help.item.preset-editor-cancel: Close this preset editor without saving its changes.
help.item.preset-editor-submit: Save the entered preset name and description.
help.item.prompt-preview-close: Close the prompt preview without changing the current prompt settings.
help.item.readalong-cancel-btn: Request cancellation of the read-along sidecar build.
help.item.readalong-include-text: Include the script text in the downloadable sidecar. Unchecked sidecars contain timings only.
help.item.readaloud-cancel-btn: Request cancellation of the EPUB read-aloud build.
help.item.roster-add: Add a character with a new identity to the draft. Supply its name and supporting source quote.
help.item.roster-approve: Approve the exact reviewed draft for future script generation and save one exact undo. Changed inputs refuse approval.
help.item.roster-discard: Explicitly remove the saved undo while keeping the current cast and roster. Resolve it before another approval.
help.item.roster-export: Download the approved character identities and evidence. Unsaved draft edits are excluded.
help.item.roster-load: Load the selected source, cast, approved identities and saved undo. After an unconfirmed write, inspect saved state before another action.
help.item.roster-merge: Merge selected draft characters into the chosen surviving identity. Review aliases and evidence before approval.
help.item.roster-next: Show the next page of draft characters.
help.item.roster-preview: Check identity decisions and exact quotes against current saved inputs. Preview does not approve or change the cast.
help.item.roster-previous: Show the previous page of draft characters.
help.item.roster-recover: Restore the previous unsaved draft for this source and saved roster, then review it again.
help.item.roster-retire: Remove selected characters from the draft while retaining their retired identity history after approval.
help.item.roster-seed: Start an empty identity draft from this source’s current cast. Add and locate supporting quotes before approval.
help.item.roster-split: Split one selected character into separate identities. Review each resulting character’s name and supporting quotes.
help.item.roster-undo: Restore the cast and roster from before the last approval. Changed source or approved files prevent an unsafe rollback.
help.item.script-batch-narrator: Exact character name to use as narrator for this book in the batch. Leave blank to use the normal narrator assignment.
help.item.script-recovery-compare: Source text or batch entries for the failed chunk. Compare these with the replacement model reply.
help.item.script-recovery-inject: Paste a replacement model reply for the failed chunk, then validate it before applying it.
help.item.section-collapse: Show or hide this section’s additional settings.
help.item.settings-llm-advanced-toggle: Show or hide request timeouts and retry backoff for the selected LLM location. Expanding this group does not change its settings.
help.item.speaker-review-cancel: Request cancellation of the current speaker-label review.
help.item.speaker-review-cancel-previous: Request cancellation of the previous speaker-label review still running.
help.item.speaker-review-load: Refresh available label-review sources and saved references.
help.item.speaker-review-preview: Preview speaker-label disagreements and the excerpts that a review would send to the model.
help.item.speaker-review-refresh: Refresh the status and result of this speaker-label review.
help.item.speaker-review-start: Start the previewed speaker-label review after the required source/reference consent.
help.item.stale-build-dismiss: Dismiss the notice about changed app files without reloading the page.
help.item.summary-toggle: Show or hide the details described by this heading.
help.item.task-log-download: Download the full task log for troubleshooting.
help.item.toast-undo: Undo the recently deleted script line while this undo action remains available.

Proposal only: never changes the Script, source, or any language setting, and it refuses rather than download when Argos needs a sentence-splitter model that is not already installed. It belongs to the active book; re-opening the panel with nothing running shows the most recent saved preview for the current book, and another book's preview is never shown for this book.
help.item.translated-edition-refresh: Re-check which language pairs are installed on this machine. Does not download anything.

help.item.workspace-collection-show: Show progress for the selected saved books without opening, loading or changing any book.

script.translated-edition.intro: Build a reviewable translation proposal for the first 25 saved Script rows in one installed language pair, for authorised source material. The result is a proposal, not an approved translation: it never replaces the Script or source, adds no audio, and changes no UI, source or TTS language. Nothing is downloaded and no text leaves this machine: only directly installed pairs are listed (listing them fetches no index or package), and a preview refuses to start rather than let Argos fetch a sentence-splitting model (when a missing model is the cause, the refusal names the file). A proposal belongs to the active book: re-opening this panel shows the most recent saved preview for the current book, if one is still on disk (rebuild if the Script changed; a preview that is still building keeps showing its own progress), and a preview from another book is never shown for this book. Loading a different saved book from the library removes the previous folder; selecting an uploaded source leaves old files on disk until a different-book library load, and those files are never shown for the new book. Saving the book to the library does not copy proposals into the saved book.

setup.strategy.three-steps.help: Turning a book into a script happens in three steps, for one book or a batch alike: 1 split the text into narration and spoken lines, 2 decide who says each line, 3 write a delivery note for each line. The settings below control how much text the AI sees in all three steps. The defaults are what this project's published accuracy numbers were measured with; change them to trade speed for context.
setup.strategy.tp-attribute-batch-size.h: How many lines (narration and dialogue) the AI looks at together when deciding who speaks. More lines per request means more of the scene in view but longer replies; 25 is the tested default.
setup.strategy.tp-attribute-context-char: Also show the AI this much of the book before and after the lines it is deciding on, for context only (it is told not to assign speakers to it). 0 = off. Every 1,000 characters adds roughly 300 tokens to each request, so it costs time (and money on paid APIs). Whether it improves accuracy is being measured; see RECIPES.md.
Step 2: extra text around each request (characters, each side)
setup.strategy.tp-attribute-target-chars: 0 keeps existing line-based batching. A positive value targets complete source entries, excluding extra context. Requests may be smaller to fit the selected model; a single entry can exceed this target. Larger targets do not increase the loaded model context.
setup.strategy.tp-chunk-size.help: How much of the book is sent per request when splitting it into lines. Bigger pieces mean fewer requests, but the AI has to write every word back, so its reply grows with the piece, and if one word comes back wrong the whole piece is redone. If a piece is too big for the model to write back in one reply, generation stops before it starts and tells you a size that fits.
setup.strategy.tp-chunk-size.label: Step 1: text per request (characters)
setup.strategy.tp-delivery-direction.hel: The experimental modes ask the model to direct how each line answers the one before it and to mark pauses (a beat, a cut-off, trailing off) that become silence between lines. They are being evaluated in a blind listening test and are off by default. They need the default Step 3 prompt preset. Changing this restarts an unfinished book instead of resuming it.
setup.strategy.tp-group-rule-help.help: Assign unnamed group dialogue to the listed group name instead of UNKNOWN; this is off by default.
setup.strategy.tp-group-rule.label: Listed groups answer for their members
setup.strategy.tp-instruct-context-chars: Zero adds no extra prose. Adds contiguous text outside the request's first and last target, beyond boundary entries already supplied as context. Text is clipped at the character limit. Sparse targets retain their immediate neighbours in the request. The full prompt must fit the model's input and context limits; delivery quality has not been measured.
Step 3: extra text around each request (characters, each side)
0 keeps existing line-based batching. A positive value targets complete source entries, excluding extra context. Requests may be smaller to fit the selected model; a single entry can exceed this target. Larger targets do not increase the loaded model context.

Compact labels sends numbered sentences and asks the model for a label per sentence instead of rewriting the text; if a reply is unusable or fails the fidelity check, that chunk falls back to Full text automatically. In testing (#744) it used fewer output tokens and failed fewer chunks on messy formats, but scored a little lower on clean single-quote books. Changing this restarts an unfinished book instead of resuming it.

setup.strategy.tp-segmentation.help: Quote marks first uses the quote marks where the text makes it clear which parts are speech and asks the model about the rest. Quote marks only never asks the model: anything inside quote marks is dialogue, everything else is narration. Quote-aware is the same deterministic split but treats strongly signalled quoted terms (for example, “known as X”) as narration. Model only always asks the model.

training.help.alpha: Scaling factor for LoRA weights. Effective strength = alpha / rank. Higher alpha relative to rank means the adapter has more influence. A common starting point is alpha = 2x rank.
training.help.batch-size: Samples processed per step. Limited by VRAM. Batch 1 with gradient accumulation is typical for 24GB cards.
training.help.data: Sample count is inventory, not a quality score. Inspect recording consistency and the retained evaluation probes; compare Clone and LoRA by listening because neither mode won consistently across tested voices.

training.help.epochs: Number of full passes over the dataset. Too many can overfit; too few can underfit, but the experiments did not establish a universal range. Use retained checkpoint evaluation and blind listening rather than sample count or training loss alone.
training.help.grad-accum: Simulates larger batches by accumulating gradients over N steps before updating. Effective batch = batch_size x grad_accum. Higher values give smoother training at the cost of speed.
training.help.language: Sets the codec language prefix token used during training. Must match the language of your training audio. For unsupported languages, try "english" as a proxy.
training.help.lr: Step size for weight updates. Default 1e-6 is conservative. Higher rates (5e-6 or 1e-5) train faster but risk instability.
training.help.rank.high-tail: captures voice identity strongly but can override the model's ability to follow instruct/style prompts, producing flat delivery.
training.help.rank.low-tail: preserves expressiveness and instruct-following but captures less voice detail. Start with 16-32 for a balance.
